title: Coordinate points and values of the standard additive and multiplicative groups
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $R$ be a commutative $k$-algebra, and use the standard group schemes $\mathbf G_a=\operatorname{Spec}k[y]$ and $\mathbf G_m=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$ of [def-sc-gm-ga], including their affine spectra and contravariant coordinate maps. For $x\in R$, define the additive coordinate point $a_x:\operatorname{Spec}R\to\mathbf G_a$ to be the $k$-scheme morphism induced by the $k$-algebra homomorphism $k[y]\to R$ sending $y$ to $x$. For a $k$-scheme morphism $g:\operatorname{Spec}R\to\mathbf G_m$, let $g^*:k[t,t^{-1}]\to R$ be its corresponding $k$-algebra homomorphism and define its multiplicative coordinate value to be $g^*(t)\in R$. This value is a unit because $g^*(t^{-1})$ is its inverse. These definitions allow the zero algebra and nonreduced algebras.
